sources.entry: Beets - Music library manager and MusicBrainz tagger (command-line and Web interface). (Source Code) MIT Python/deb
beets - A music library manager and MusicBrainz tagger.
Beets | Music library manager and MusicBrainz tagger

summary.one_liner: Beets is a command-line music library manager that catalogs audio collections and automatically corrects and enriches their metadata, using MusicBrainz and other sources.
summary.what_it_does: Beets imports music into a library database and uses a tag corrector to fix track, album, and artist metadata, matching against MusicBrainz and other sources such as Discogs and Beatport. Plugins extend it to fetch album art, lyrics, genres, tempos, ReplayGain levels, and acoustic fingerprints. It can transcode audio to other formats, find duplicate tracks and albums or albums with missing tracks, and embed or extract album art. The README also describes a web interface for browsing the library and playing it in an HTML5-capable browser, and support for MPD-compatible music players. Users can write their own plugins in Python.
use_cases: organize and tag a music collection
fix incorrect or messy music metadata
download album art and lyrics automatically
find duplicate songs or incomplete albums
transcode music library to another format
browse and play a music library in a web browser
serve a library to MPD-compatible music players
how_to_run: Or install directly from GitHub (see the Install section of the README)
beet import ~/music/ (run the import command on a music folder)
notable: Automatic tag correction during import, with similarity scores for matches
Plugin system covering art, lyrics, genres, tempos, ReplayGain, and fingerprints
Built-in web interface for browsing and playing the library in a browser
Duplicate and missing-track detection across the library
caveats: Command-line driven; the README shows terminal usage as the main workflow
Extra features depend on plugins, which the README does not detail
